title: Part (I): existence, characterization, uniqueness, mass bound Λ^k·M(X) and support of the Lipschitz push-forward of a normal current, from the reference sequences and the comparison lemma (supplied Steps 2–6)
statement: Notation: ℝ^p := Eucl p; D_q(ℝ^p) := GeometricCurrentOn univ q and D^q(ℝ^p) := TestFormOn univ q; M = mass, spt = support, ∂ = boundary; for a test form φ, dφ := exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ q φ, whose underlying form is exteriorDerivative φ; |γ| := covectorEuclideanNorm γ; A_ρ := thickening ρ A; C^∞ means ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞); a map g is proper on F if g⁻¹(K) ∩ F is compact for every compact K. For g : ℝ^p → ℝ^q, ω ∈ D^j(ℝ^q), η ∈ D^j(ℝ^p) and A ⊆ ℝ^p, 'η is compatible with (g, ω) near A' means: there is an open N ⊇ A with η(x) = ω(g(x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ g x) for all x ∈ N. For X ∈ D_k(ℝ^m), G : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} and S ∈ D_k(ℝ^{m′}), LipPF(X, G, S) means: for every sequence (G_n) of C^∞ maps ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, every open O ⊇ spt X and every L ∈ ℝ such that eventually ‖fderiv ℝ G_n x‖ ≤ L for all x ∈ O, and G_n → G uniformly on O, and for every ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^{m′}) and every sequence (η_n) in D^k(ℝ^m) such that eventually η_n is compatible with (G_n, ω) near spt X, the sequence X(η_n) converges to S(ω). Assume (RS): for all m, m′ ∈ ℕ, G : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, Λ ∈ ℝ≥0, r ∈ ℝ and F ⊆ ℝ^m such that r > 0, F is closed, G is Λ-Lipschitz on F_r and G is proper on F, there are C^∞ maps G_n : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} (n ∈ ℕ) with ‖fderiv ℝ G_n x‖ ≤ Λ for all n and all x ∈ F_{r/2}, G_n → G uniformly on F_{r/2}, and G_n proper on F for all sufficiently large n (this is the conclusion of the sibling reference_sequence); and (CL): for all m, m′, k ∈ ℕ, every X ∈ D_k(ℝ^m) with M(X) < ∞ such that M(∂Y) < ∞ for every j ∈ ℕ and Y ∈ D_{j+1}(ℝ^m) with k = j + 1 and HEq Y X, every G : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} proper on spt X, all sequences (G_n), (G′_n) of C^∞ maps ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, all open O, O′ ⊇ spt X and all L, L′ ∈ ℝ such that eventually ‖fderiv ℝ G_n x‖ ≤ L for all x ∈ O and eventually ‖fderiv ℝ G′_n x‖ ≤ L′ for all x ∈ O′, G_n → G uniformly on O and G′_n → G uniformly on O′, every ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^{m′}) and all sequences (η_n), (η′_n) in D^k(ℝ^m) such that eventually η_n is compatible with (G_n, ω) near spt X and eventually η′_n is compatible with (G′_n, ω) near spt X: X(η′_n) − X(η_n) → 0 (this is the conclusion of the sibling comparison). Then the following holds: (I) For all m, m′, k ∈ ℕ, X ∈ D_k(ℝ^m) with M(X) < ∞ such that M(∂Y) < ∞ for every j ∈ ℕ and Y ∈ D_{j+1}(ℝ^m) with k = j + 1 and HEq Y X, G : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, Λ ∈ ℝ≥0 and r > 0 such that G is Λ-Lipschitz on thickening r (spt X) and G⁻¹(K) ∩ spt X is compact for every compact K: there is S ∈ D_k(ℝ^{m′}) with LipPF(X, G, S) such that every S′ ∈ D_k(ℝ^{m′}) with LipPF(X, G, S′) equals S, M(S) ≤ Λ^k·M(X) (in ℝ≥0∞) and spt S ⊆ closure(G(spt X)).
